name: Speed up Test CI job on GitHub-hosted runners

description: Baseline hosted-CI Test job on current main with CI maxWorkers at 50%

asi.hypothesis: Establish a fresh hosted-runner baseline for the complete Test job before changing worker concurrency.
asi.historical_context: The 847s baseline is within the predecessor PR's 723-854s range; package coverage remains dominant at 668s.

description: Raise CI Vitest workers from 50% to 75%, leaving one hosted-runner core free

asi.hypothesis: Using three of four hosted-runner cores should shorten the dominant coverage phase while preserving one core for Postgres and orchestration.
asi.result: The complete Test job improved by 60s (7.1%); the package coverage phase improved by 61s while examples and startup were unchanged. No instability appeared in this run.
asi.next_action_hint: Test 100% workers to find whether the fourth worker helps or recreates oversubscription.

description: Use all four hosted-runner cores for CI Vitest workers

asi.hypothesis: A fourth Vitest worker might further reduce the package coverage phase.
asi.result: Coverage was only 3s faster than 75%, while startup rose 9s and the complete job regressed 7s. The fourth worker provides no primary-metric benefit and removes resource headroom.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from the 787s best to 794s and full concurrency has higher stability risk.
asi.next_action_hint: Restore 75%; inspect CI logs for per-project durations or test independent phase overlap.

description: Run CI Vitest projects in worker threads at the winning 75% concurrency

asi.hypothesis: Threads could reduce process startup and module-transfer overhead across 1,164 test files while retaining isolation.
asi.result: The suite passed, but the complete job was 3s slower and coverage 6s slower than the 75%-fork run; thread startup savings did not offset execution cost.
asi.rollback_reason: No primary metric improvement over 75% with the default fork pool.
asi.next_action_hint: Restore 75% forks; test overlap of independent package coverage and example workloads or inspect typecheck/import dominance.

description: Run package coverage and example tests concurrently inside the Test job

asi.hypothesis: Overlapping the independent package-coverage and example-test commands should reduce wall time despite CPU contention, while preserving one Test job and all pass/fail guarantees.
asi.result: The full job improved from 787s to 703s (10.7%). Contention slowed coverage from 607s to 638s and examples from 114s to 191s, but 191s of overlap more than compensated. Both workloads and coverage reporting passed.
asi.correctness: The shell waits for both PIDs, preserves either exit status, emits phase timing, and the existing coverage report still runs under !cancelled(). The workflow contract test was updated and passes.
asi.next_action_hint: Try 50% coverage workers during overlap to reduce contention, or confirm the 703s result before increasing complexity.

description: Reserve two hosted-runner cores for example tests during workload overlap

asi.hypothesis: Reducing package Vitest from three to two workers during overlap might lessen contention enough to shorten the combined critical path.
asi.result: Both workloads slowed: coverage rose to 668s and examples to 242s, producing a 748s job, 45s worse than 75% overlap.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed 6.4%; reserving an extra core did not improve effective throughput.
asi.next_action_hint: Restore 75% overlap. Try 100% overlap only as a boundary check, though prior serial 100% had no benefit.

description: Use full CI Vitest concurrency while package coverage overlaps example tests

asi.hypothesis: With examples already consuming otherwise idle intervals, allowing Vitest its fourth worker may increase total throughput despite oversubscription.
asi.result: The job dropped from 703s to 548s (22.0%); coverage fell from 638s to 475s while examples stayed near 196s. All 1,164 package files, examples, coverage report, and clean-tree check passed.
asi.risk: This is unexpectedly much better than both 75%-overlap and serial 100%. Full concurrency previously carried Postgres/PGlite instability risk, so repeat before trusting.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat the identical 100%-overlap configuration to test stability and timing reproducibility.

description: Repeat full-concurrency overlap configuration for reproducibility

asi.hypothesis: An unchanged rerun would confirm the 548s result and full-concurrency stability.
asi.result: The rerun passed but took 739s; coverage varied from 475s to 663s and examples from 196s to 248s. Hosted-runner variance is much larger than expected, so the 548s point is not representative by itself.
asi.rollback_reason: The repeated measurement regressed 191s versus the prior point; no code delta exists to retain or revert.
asi.next_action_hint: Run another unchanged 100%-overlap sample, then compare a small sample distribution against repeated 75%-overlap rather than single minima.

description: Third full-concurrency overlap measurement

asi.hypothesis: A third sample would distinguish the 548s outlier from typical 100%-overlap performance.
asi.result: The job passed at 735s, nearly matching the 739s repeat. Typical full-concurrency overlap is therefore about 737s; the 548s run was a favorable hosted-runner outlier.
asi.rollback_reason: No code delta; this repeated point is worse than both the retained minimum and the sole 75%-overlap sample.
asi.next_action_hint: Switch back to 75%-overlap and collect two more samples for a fair median comparison.

description: Return to 75%-worker overlap for a second sample

asi.hypothesis: Leaving one core free should make overlap faster and steadier than full Vitest concurrency.
asi.result: The second 75% sample passed at 736s versus its first 703s sample. Coverage was 661s and examples 195s. This is effectively tied with the two typical 100% samples at 735s and 739s.
asi.rollback_reason: The 736s primary metric did not improve the retained best; the tool cannot meaningfully revert already-pushed measurement commits.
asi.next_action_hint: Collect a third 75% sample; choose based on medians and stability, not the 548s outlier.

description: Third 75%-worker overlap measurement

asi.hypothesis: A third 75% sample would establish a robust median for selecting worker concurrency.
asi.result: The run passed at 571s. Three 75% samples are 571/703/736 (median 703s); three 100% samples are 548/735/739 (median 735s). Choose 75% based on the 32s lower median and resource headroom.
asi.rollback_reason: This sample does not beat the absolute 548s hosted-runner outlier, though it establishes 75% as the better median configuration.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep 75% conceptually and cap concurrent example Turbo task concurrency; examples finish far before coverage, so trading example speed for less coverage contention may reduce the critical path.

description: Limit overlapping example Turbo tasks to one at a time

asi.hypothesis: Serializing example workspace tasks would free CPU for the coverage critical path while examples still finish before coverage.
asi.result: The job passed at 674s; examples expanded to 333s but still completed 266s before coverage at 599s. This is 29s below the uncapped 75%-overlap median, but one sample cannot resolve runner noise.
asi.rollback_reason: The single 674s point does not beat the retained absolute best and requires comparison with a moderate example concurrency.
asi.next_action_hint: Try --concurrency=2, which may reduce examples oversubscription without serializing all workspace tasks.

description: Limit overlapping example Turbo tasks to two at a time

asi.hypothesis: Two concurrent example workspace tasks could balance example completion against package-coverage CPU needs.
asi.result: The job passed but took 763s; coverage was the slowest overlap sample at 686s while examples took 246s. Moderate Turbo concurrency did not produce a useful balance.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed 89s versus example concurrency 1 and 60s versus uncapped 75%-overlap median.
asi.next_action_hint: Return to concurrency 1 for another sample, or test whether deferring examples until late in coverage can reduce peak contention.

description: Repeat single-example-task overlap configuration

asi.hypothesis: A second concurrency-1 sample would confirm its apparent lower overlap median.
asi.result: The Test job failed: postgres-codec-testkit aggregate defaults lost its database connection (`read ECONNRESET`, then `Client has encountered a connection error and is not queryable`), causing 7 failures. Examples completed in 245s; package coverage failed after 555s.
asi.error_details: Hosted-run log also showed react-router Postgres pool connection terminations. This matches the resource-starvation failure mode documented by the original 50% worker cap.
asi.rollback_reason: Parallel package coverage and example tests introduce unacceptable Postgres flakiness even at 75% package workers and example concurrency 1.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon workload overlap, restore serial examples, retain 75% package workers, and collect repeated serial 75% measurements.

description: Restore serial workloads and retain 75% package Vitest workers after overlap flake

asi.hypothesis: Serializing examples again removes database contention while three Vitest workers preserve the safe package-coverage speedup.
asi.result: The full Test job passed in 773s, 74s (8.7%) below the 847s baseline. Package coverage took 585s versus baseline 668s; examples returned to 111s.
asi.correctness: This removes the overlap configuration that produced ECONNRESET and returns to the established step-level failure semantics.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat serial 75% once more for stability, then investigate coverage-specific settings that do not add concurrent database load.

description: Repeat serial 75%-worker configuration for stability

asi.hypothesis: A repeated serial 75% run would confirm the worker-count speedup without the overlap flake.
asi.result: All 1,164 files and 15,364 tests passed, but Vitest failed the phase because language-server/server.test.ts produced an unhandled `Connection is disposed` rejection after its final test. Coverage reporting and examples still passed.
asi.error_details: Unlike the overlap failure, this was not a Postgres connection loss. It is an asynchronous language-server teardown race and may be an existing suite flake, but increased file concurrency could increase its likelihood.
asi.rollback_reason: A speedup that raises CI flake risk is not acceptable without distinguishing or fixing the teardown race.
asi.next_action_hint: Test isolate:false at the safe 50% worker cap, using Vitest's own report that 998 worker spawns cost at least ~43.75s; shared-state failures will reveal whether it is viable.

description: Reuse CI Vitest workers across files at the safe 50% concurrency cap

asi.hypothesis: Disabling per-file worker isolation should eliminate most of the 998 worker spawns Vitest reported while retaining the stable two-worker resource cap.
asi.result: The complete job passed in 815s, 32s below baseline; package coverage improved from 668s to 641s. All tests, type tests, coverage thresholds/reporting, examples, and clean-tree checks passed.
asi.risk: Worker reuse can expose shared module/process state between files, so repeated runs are required even though this run was clean.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat isolate:false at 50% to test stability and timing.

description: Repeat 50%-worker reuse configuration

asi.hypothesis: A second isolate:false run at 50% would confirm the spawn-overhead improvement without shared-state failures.
asi.result: The run passed in 836s. Two samples are 815s and 836s (median 825.5s), only 21.5s below the 847s baseline and within broader hosted-runner variability.
asi.rollback_reason: The repeated point did not improve the retained 815s result; the small apparent gain does not yet justify global loss of file isolation.
asi.next_action_hint: Try isolate:false with 75% workers to see whether reuse also prevents the language-server teardown race while retaining higher throughput.

description: Combine three CI workers with cross-file worker reuse

asi.hypothesis: Worker reuse at 75% could preserve higher throughput and avoid the prior per-file teardown rejection.
asi.result: The job passed in 802s, 45s below baseline and 13s below the best 50%-reuse sample. Coverage took 613s. No language-server or database error occurred.
asi.risk: Global isolate:false remains a semantic tradeoff and this timing is slower than successful isolate:true 75% samples.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat for stability; discard isolate:false if it does not demonstrate a clear repeatable advantage over simpler 75% isolation.

description: Repeat three-worker CI with cross-file worker reuse

asi.hypothesis: A second 75%-reuse run would show whether the configuration is stable and repeatably faster than baseline.
asi.result: The job passed in 781s. Two samples are 802s and 781s (median 791.5s), with package coverage at 613s and 603s. No unhandled rejection or database loss occurred.
asi.tradeoff: The median is ~55s below baseline but only modestly different from 75% with isolation, while shared process state is a broader semantic change.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate targeted isolate:false only for packages without stateful/database tests, or retain isolation and optimize worker spawning another way.

description: Drop redundant text coverage reporter at the safe 50% worker cap

asi.hypothesis: The custom JSON coverage gate makes Vitest's huge text table redundant; emitting only JSON should reduce report generation/log transport while restoring safe isolation and worker count.
asi.result: The complete job passed in 742s, 105s below baseline; package coverage took 552s. The magnitude exceeds expected reporter savings and likely includes favorable runner variance.
asi.correctness: Coverage JSON was generated, the custom per-package report passed, examples passed, and file isolation plus the original 50% resource cap were restored.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat unchanged to estimate the true reporter-only gain.

description: Repeat JSON-only coverage reporter configuration

asi.hypothesis: A repeat would show a small consistent gain from avoiding text coverage rendering/logging.
asi.result: The unchanged run passed but took 945s, with coverage at 751s. Together with 742s, this confirms extreme hosted-runner variance and does not quantify a meaningful reporter-only speedup.
asi.rollback_reason: The repeated primary metric is 98s worse than baseline; no code delta exists in this measurement commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain JSON-only only if simplification is independently worthwhile; pursue structural savings with less sensitivity to runner speed.

description: Use VM-isolated fork workers at the safe 50% concurrency cap

asi.hypothesis: vmForks could reuse child processes while creating an isolated VM context per file, avoiding global shared state and most fork startup cost.
asi.result: All tests passed, but the complete job took 864s. Coverage was 635s; startup and examples were also slower than typical. No clear primary benefit appeared.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed 17s versus baseline and 122s versus the best JSON-only safe run.
asi.next_action_hint: Try vmThreads only if cross-realm/native compatibility is acceptable; otherwise remove VM pooling and focus on CI step structure or coverage output.

description: Use VM-isolated thread workers at the safe 50% concurrency cap

asi.hypothesis: vmThreads should preserve per-file isolation while avoiding per-file process spawn overhead more efficiently than vmForks.
asi.result: The complete job passed in 819s, 45s faster than vmForks and 28s below baseline. Coverage took 641s. No cross-realm or native/WASM failure appeared.
asi.rollback_reason: The single result did not beat the retained safe JSON-only minimum and is close to normal runner variation.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat unchanged to test vmThreads stability and estimate its median.

description: Repeat VM-isolated thread workers at 50% CI concurrency

asi.hypothesis: A second vmThreads run would confirm stable isolated worker reuse.
asi.result: The job passed again in 814s, nearly identical to 819s; coverage was 640s versus 641s. The 816.5s median is 30.5s below baseline and materially steadier than default-fork hosted samples.
asi.correctness: vmThreads creates a fresh VM context per file, so file-level module/global isolation remains. Supabase explicitly overrides the root pool to forks for its WASM/mock requirements.
asi.risk: VM realms can change instanceof identity and memory behavior; two complete passes found no incompatibility, but a third pass is prudent.
asi.next_action_hint: Run a third vmThreads sample, then consider vmMemoryLimit or 75% vmThreads if stability remains clean.

description: Third VM-thread isolation stability run

asi.hypothesis: A third vmThreads pass would rule out immediate cross-realm, memory, and flake concerns.
asi.result: The third run passed in 811s with coverage at 636s. Three samples are 819/814/811 (median 814s, 8s range), the most stable candidate distribution in the session.
asi.correctness: All 1,164 files, 15,364 tests, type tests, JSON coverage collection, custom thresholds, examples, and clean-tree checks passed for a third time.
asi.next_action_hint: Test vmThreads at 75% workers; the VM pool may avoid process oversubscription while using the third core.

description: Run VM-isolated CI tests with three workers

asi.hypothesis: A third VM-thread worker can improve throughput without the fork/process pressure that motivated the original 50% cap.
asi.result: The full job passed in 753s, 58s faster than the best 50%-vmThreads sample and 94s below baseline. Coverage took 581s; examples and startup were unchanged.
asi.risk: Higher concurrency previously exposed a language-server teardown race under fork isolation, so vmThreads 75% needs repeated stability proof.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat 75%-vmThreads at least twice; reject on any unhandled rejection, database loss, or memory failure.

description: Second three-worker VM-thread stability run

asi.hypothesis: The 75%-vmThreads configuration would repeat without the fork-pool teardown/resource failures.
asi.result: The second run passed in 767s; coverage took 588s. Two samples are 753s and 767s, both substantially below the 814s median at 50% vmThreads.
asi.rollback_reason: The repeated point is 14s slower than the retained 753s minimum; no code delta exists.
asi.next_action_hint: Collect a third stability sample before selecting 75%-vmThreads.

description: Third three-worker VM-thread stability run

asi.hypothesis: A third 75%-vmThreads run would complete cleanly and establish a robust distribution.
asi.result: The third run passed in 789s. Coverage was fastest at 554s, but unrelated startup/examples noise raised total time. Three samples are 753/767/789 (median 767s), all successful.
asi.rollback_reason: The 789s point did not improve the retained minimum; no code delta exists.
asi.next_action_hint: 75%-vmThreads now has three clean samples. Test 100% vmThreads as a boundary, then choose 75% unless four workers improve repeatably.

description: First four-worker VM-thread run; measurement API transient

asi.hypothesis: Four VM-thread workers might improve coverage without fork-process pressure.
asi.result: The hosted Test job itself succeeded in 741s (coverage 568s, examples 111s), but measure.sh exited on a transient GitHub Jobs API HTTP 502 before recording metrics.
asi.error_details: Manual recovery from run 32504039496 confirmed Test success from 16:40:08Z to 16:52:29Z. This is a harness failure, not a candidate failure.
asi.rollback_reason: Log as crash because run_experiment exited nonzero and emitted no structured primary metric; do not treat the recovered single point as retained evidence.
asi.next_action_hint: Make measure.sh retry transient gh API failures, then rerun 100%-vmThreads.

description: Repeat four-worker VM-thread configuration with API retries

asi.hypothesis: A retried measurement would validate the manually recovered 741s four-worker VM result.
asi.result: The second Test job passed in 761s; coverage took 583s. Together with the recovered 741s run, 100%-vmThreads is currently ~16s faster in median than 75%-vmThreads.
asi.rollback_reason: The structured 761s point did not improve the retained 742s minimum; no code delta exists in this measurement commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Collect a third 100%-vmThreads stability sample before choosing between 100% and 75%.

description: Third four-worker VM-thread stability run

asi.hypothesis: A third four-worker VM run would establish stable throughput without database or teardown failures.
asi.result: The third run passed in 752s. Three complete jobs are 741/761/752 (median 752s, 20s range), versus 753/767/789 (median 767s) at 75% and 819/814/811 (median 814s) at 50%.
asi.correctness: No Postgres, PGlite, language-server, cross-realm, or memory failure occurred across all three 100%-vmThreads jobs.
asi.decision: Select 100%-vmThreads: it preserves per-file VM isolation, honors Supabase's explicit forks/maxWorkers override, and has the best stable candidate median.
asi.next_action_hint: Test whether JSON-only coverage output materially contributes by restoring the text reporter under the selected VM configuration for an A/B sample.

description: Restore text coverage diagnostics under selected VM-thread configuration

asi.hypothesis: A/B with the text reporter restored would show whether JSON-only output contributes to the speedup.
asi.result: The job passed in 772s. Vitest reported 587.58s while the API coverage step was 591s, a 3.42s tail; JSON-only had a 565.39s Vitest duration and 569s API step, a 3.61s tail. Text rendering adds no measurable post-suite cost.
asi.rollback_reason: The 772s primary point is slower than the selected JSON-only samples, but phase-internal evidence attributes that to runner execution variance, not the text reporter.
asi.decision: Restore the text reporter to preserve existing diagnostics and keep the final product diff focused on worker pool/concurrency only.
asi.next_action_hint: Now optimize startup or test execution structurally; do not revisit coverage reporter output.

description: Start Cloudflare example Postgres after package coverage

asi.hypothesis: Deferring the example-only 5433 Postgres container would keep it from competing with the 9-minute package coverage phase.
asi.result: The job passed in 812s. Coverage took 574s, essentially the same as the selected 100%-vmThreads median (569s); Cloudflare startup took 11s after coverage. Example time was an unrelated 156s outlier.
asi.rollback_reason: No primary improvement in the first sample; total time regressed due example/startup runner noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat once because coverage stayed near the selected median and the resource-lifetime reduction is logically sound.

description: Repeat deferred Cloudflare startup under four VM workers

asi.hypothesis: A second deferred-container sample would isolate whether removing idle Postgres competition helps coverage.
asi.result: All 1,165 files and 15,375 tests passed, but the coverage step failed on the known language-server teardown race: an unhandled `Connection is disposed` rejection after the final pull-diagnostics test. Coverage execution was 576.75s.
asi.error_details: This is the second occurrence across different pool configurations, so it is a benchmark-independent test harness teardown defect rather than evidence against deferred Cloudflare startup.
asi.rollback_reason: Any CI failure is unacceptable; no performance result can be kept from this run.
asi.next_action_hint: Add a graceful harness shutdown path that awaits an LSP ShutdownRequest before disposal, while retaining immediate dispose for tests that deliberately settle work after teardown.

description: Drain language-server JSON-RPC before test harness disposal

asi.hypothesis: Awaiting the standard LSP ShutdownRequest before routine harness disposal will drain queued JSON-RPC writes and eliminate the intermittent post-test `Connection is disposed` rejection.
asi.result: The complete CI Test job passed in 792s after the fix; the language-server package also passed locally with 261 tests. No unhandled rejection occurred.
asi.correctness: Immediate `dispose()` remains available for tests that deliberately settle a load after teardown; normal afterEach uses the new graceful `shutdown()`. A regression test covers shutdown after pull diagnostics.
asi.scope_note: This stabilizes the test harness rather than weakening Vitest unhandled-error handling or retrying failed tests.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat the exact configuration to verify the teardown race stays absent; then decide whether deferred Cloudflare startup has value.

description: Repeat graceful LSP teardown with four VM workers

asi.hypothesis: The teardown fix and selected VM-thread configuration would pass repeatedly.
asi.result: The second post-fix job passed in 761s, with coverage at 582s. Both post-fix runs completed without the formerly intermittent language-server unhandled rejection.
asi.stability: Across the broader 100%-vmThreads set, five successful timing samples now cluster around a 761s upper median; the single teardown failure has a targeted fix and two subsequent clean runs.
asi.next_action_hint: Run a third post-fix sample for confidence, then A/B deferred Cloudflare startup by moving it back while retaining VM threads and graceful teardown.

description: Third post-fix stability sample blocked by SSH transport

asi.hypothesis: A third post-fix hosted run would provide final teardown stability confidence.
asi.result: No CI run started. The measurement commit succeeded locally, but `git push` failed immediately because github.com closed the SSH connection.
asi.error_details: `fatal: the remote end hung up upon initial contact`; this is external transport failure, not candidate behavior.
asi.rollback_reason: No hosted benchmark exists for this iteration.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry the unchanged configuration; the next measure commit will include and push the local unpushed commit.

description: Third post-fix graceful-teardown stability run

asi.hypothesis: The third actual post-fix job would remain free of language-server teardown failures.
asi.result: The job passed in 772s with coverage at 580s. Three post-fix jobs (792/761/772) all passed, establishing the graceful shutdown fix as stable under four VM workers.
asi.rollback_reason: The 772s point is 11s slower than the retained post-fix minimum; no code delta exists.
asi.next_action_hint: A/B Cloudflare startup position now that pool and teardown are stable.

description: Cloudflare startup A/B blocked by GitHub API timeout

asi.hypothesis: Restoring Cloudflare startup to its original position would test whether deferral changes performance.
asi.result: The branch pushed and CI likely triggered, but measure.sh failed while listing workflows due a GitHub API TLS handshake timeout before discovering the run.
asi.error_details: `couldn't fetch workflows ... net/http: TLS handshake timeout`
asi.rollback_reason: No benchmark result was acquired in the experiment cycle.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry run discovery API failures in measure.sh and recover or rerun the exact SHA.

description: Cloudflare startup A/B retry blocked by SSH disconnect

asi.hypothesis: Retry the original Cloudflare startup ordering benchmark after hardening API discovery.
asi.result: No hosted run started because the SSH push connection was closed by GitHub after a long network stall.
asi.error_details: `fatal: Could not read from remote repository` after 2015s wall time.
asi.rollback_reason: External transport failure produced no metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry push/measurement when GitHub SSH recovers; consider adding bounded push retries/timeouts to the harness.

description: Restore original Cloudflare Postgres startup ordering

asi.hypothesis: Starting Cloudflare Postgres before coverage would A/B whether deferral affected the critical path.
asi.result: The job passed in 776s with coverage at 590s. This is effectively tied with deferred-start post-fix samples (median 772s); moving an idle container did not produce a measurable benefit.
asi.rollback_reason: The point did not improve the retained 761s result.
asi.decision: Keep the original workflow ordering to minimize the final product diff; the optimization is entirely in Vitest pooling/concurrency, plus the teardown stabilization it required.
asi.next_action_hint: Update session notes, then test another independent Vitest setting or prepare the selected minimal diff.

description: Use vmThreads default concurrency without a redundant 100% cap

asi.hypothesis: Vitest's default worker count equals 100% of available CPUs, so removing the explicit cap should preserve performance with a smaller, clearer config change.
asi.result: The job passed in 763s, effectively equal to the 761s retained run. Coverage took 590s, within the selected pool's normal range.
asi.simplicity: The final config now changes only the CI pool. The comment accurately explains VM per-file isolation and package-level overrides instead of claiming 100% is a cap.
asi.next_action_hint: Try VM pool memory recycling only if logs show growth; otherwise the minimal one-line pool change is the strongest final candidate.

description: Restore all-core VM-thread concurrency after teardown stabilization

asi.hypothesis: Explicit 100% worker concurrency should outperform Vitest's default CPU-minus-one policy now that VM isolation and graceful teardown are stable.
asi.result: The job passed in 704s, the fastest safe serial-workload result. Package coverage fell to 478s; examples were a slower 155s, so the primary improvement came entirely from package execution.
asi.variance_note: 478s coverage is unusually favorable relative to prior 100%-vmThreads samples (568-597s), so use the established median evidence—not this minimum alone—to justify all-core concurrency.
asi.decision: Retain explicit 100%: three pre-fix all-core VM jobs had a 752s median, and the post-fix all-core runs remain clean; CPU-minus-one was 763s in its sample.
asi.next_action_hint: Update the experiment prompt with the selected result, then inspect the final diff and run repository correctness checks.

description: Prebundle SSR dependencies for package tests

asi.hypothesis: Vite SSR dependency optimization could reduce the 42-43% import share by prebundling repeatedly imported dependencies.
asi.result: The job passed but took 797s; coverage was 600s, slower than the selected VM-thread distribution. Cold prebundle work did not pay back in one CI run.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed 93s versus the latest selected run and ~45s versus the all-core VM median.
asi.next_action_hint: Remove dependency optimization. Consider import-graph changes only with per-module diagnostics, not global cold prebundling.

description: Collect Vitest import-duration diagnostics

asi.hypothesis: Import-duration instrumentation would identify a small set of module-graph hotspots behind the 42% import share.
asi.result: The job passed in 728s, but no per-import breakdown appeared for the root multi-project package run, so the instrumentation yielded no actionable hotspot data. The fast timing is consistent with runner variance.
asi.rollback_reason: Instrumentation adds config/output complexity without producing its intended diagnostic and does not beat the 704s selected minimum.
asi.next_action_hint: Remove importDurations. Avoid broad import optimization without actionable module-level evidence.

description: Run five VM-isolated workers on the four-core CI runner

asi.hypothesis: One oversubscribed VM worker can hide database/import waits in a workload split roughly evenly between test execution and imports.
asi.result: The job passed in 616s, 88s faster than the prior safe minimum. Coverage took 445s and examples 105s; no database, memory, or teardown failure occurred.
asi.risk: A fixed worker count of five assumes current runner capacity and oversubscription may reintroduce resource flakes. The first point may also be a favorable runner outlier.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat maxWorkers=5 at least twice before retaining; reject on any resource instability.

description: Second five-worker VM isolation run

asi.hypothesis: Five workers would repeat the large all-core-plus-one throughput gain.
asi.result: The second run passed in 732s with coverage at 557s. It did not reproduce the 616s outlier, but remains about 20s below the four-worker median.
asi.rollback_reason: The 732s point regressed from the retained 616s minimum; no code delta exists.
asi.next_action_hint: Collect a third five-worker sample to compare medians and resource stability against four workers.

description: Third five-worker VM isolation stability run

asi.hypothesis: A third five-worker run would establish oversubscription stability.
asi.result: The run failed: adapter-postgres `rls-migration-plan.integration.test.ts` timed out at its intentional 200ms limit despite being offline. 1,164 other files passed.
asi.error_details: The package phase ran about 584s before failure. Five concurrent workers can starve a fast test's event loop enough to violate tight correctness timeouts.
asi.rollback_reason: Oversubscribing beyond runner cores introduces unacceptable timing flakes; reject maxWorkers=5 despite its faster successful runs.
asi.next_action_hint: Restore maxWorkers='100%' (four cores). Do not raise test timeouts to accommodate an optimization-induced resource flake.

description: List the serialized Supabase project first in Vitest projects
